question: Should generic local-mock normalization retain compatibility with legacy colon-containing canonical addresses, or make the new percent-encoded form an immediate strict cutover?
rationale: The collision fix is technically coherent, but strict canonical validation can stop previously accepted fixture configurations; repository evidence does not establish which upgrade contract maintainers intend.

options.title: Add a compatibility bridge
options.body: Emit the new collision-free form while accepting legacy canonical inputs through a narrowly tested read or migration path.

options.title: Accept a strict cutover
options.body: Reject legacy ambiguous forms, but document the migration and add upgrade tests that demonstrate the resulting operator-visible failures and recovery.

recommendation.title: Add a compatibility bridge
recommendation.body: Emit the new collision-free form while accepting legacy canonical inputs through a narrowly tested read or migration path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work places this person closest to the provider and channel architecture whose compatibility contract is changing.
